issue: Must a discovery violation be willful, or made in bad faith, before a trial court may exclude evidence as a sanction under Taylor v. Illinois?
provision: Taylor v. Illinois, 484 U.S. 400 (1988) (discovery-violation exclusion sanction)

sides.position: Willfulness or bad faith is a prerequisite to a lawful exclusion sanction for a discovery violation under Taylor.
cases: United States v. Peters, 937 F.2d 1422 (9th Cir. 1991)

sides.position: Willfulness is not a prerequisite to exclusion; bad faith is an important factor but not a requirement.
cases: United States v. Johnson, 970 F.2d 907 (D.C. Cir. 1992)
United States v. Pancholi, No. 24-1127 (6th Cir. 2025)

this_court: Willfulness is not a prerequisite to exclusion; the courts that have not required willfulness have the stronger argument, since Taylor did not hold willfulness is required in every case.
quote: Most relevant here, courts are divided on whether Taylor makes a “willful” discovery violation a prerequisite to a lawful exclusion.
cite: United States v. Yogesh Pancholi, No. 24-1127 (6th Cir. 2025)
